name: Chunk Data
desc: Sends a chunk section (16x16x16 blocks) with compressed block data, light values, and biome info.

fields.name: groundUpContinuous
fields.desc: True if this is a fresh chunk (sends biome + skylight)

fields.name: bitmask
fields.desc: Which 16-block sections are present (bit 0 = bottom section)

fields.name: data
fields.desc: Zlib-compressed chunk data (block IDs + block light + sky light + biomes)

notes: Each section in the bitmask contains: 4096 block IDs (2 bytes each), 2048 block light (4 bits per block), 2048 sky light (4 bits per block). For groundUp=true: 256 biome bytes at end. Data is zlib-compressed. XRay modules intercept this to replace block IDs or prevent chunk updates.

writeup.p: S21PacketChunkData carries one chunk's block, light and biome data. Server send sites: PlayerManager sends a ground-up chunk on initial load (line 365 in the corpus) and section updates with a bitmask on the chunk update tick (line 447), EntityPlayerMP sends the player's spawn chunk with bitmask 65535, and S26PacketMapChunkBulk is the multi-chunk variant. Wire layout: chunkX int, chunkZ int, groundUpContinuous bool, bitmask unsigned short, dataLength VarInt, then zlib-compressed bytes holding per-section block IDs, block light, sky light and 256 biome bytes for ground-up chunks.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleChunkData first handles unloads: a ground-up packet with bitmask 0 calls doPreChunk(false). Otherwise it invalidates the block receive region, fetches the chunk (loading it if missing), applies the extracted sections through chunk.func_177439_a, marks the range for render update, and resets relight checks for non-surface dimensions. This is the heaviest decompression and block-write path in the play state, and it runs on the client thread.

None of the 8 reference clients hook S21 in a module. The only non-vanilla corpus hit is Rise 6.1.30/6.2.4 NetworkAPI, which registers the class (clientbound index 76) so scripts can synthesize chunk packets. The XRay/Search/ChestESP entries from older docs reference Sigma 3.9, which is not in the reference set. Modules that want block data read the loaded Chunk object after vanilla applies it; rewriting chunk content would force them to decompress and re-encode the packed sections, which none of these clients does.

Cancelling S21 empties the client's view of the world while the player stays in the server world, the core of chunk-void behavior; the server never notices because there is no acknowledgement. The heavier abuse is bandwidth: PlayerManager caps per-tick chunk traffic server-side, but a plugin that floods S21 can stall a client's single-threaded handler. On the client side, Rise 6.x scripts can call receivePacket with a fabricated S21 to draw fake terrain locally, which is render-only and has no server effect.

implementation.overview: Chunk payload delivery with zero module usage in the 8 reference clients: block-aware features read the loaded world instead of hooking the packet, and the only non-vanilla reference is the Rise 6.x script registry entry.
implementation.server_handling: PlayerManager sends ground-up S21 (bitmask 0, line 365) when a player enters a chunk's watch range, and section updates (groundUp=false, line 447) on the per-chunk update tick, batching changed sections into the bitmask. EntityPlayerMP sends the spawn chunk with all 16 sections (65535). Chunk data is extracted and zlib-compressed at send time; there is no inbound handler because the packet is clientbound.
implementation.protocol_notes: Each section in the bitmask contributes 4096 block IDs at 2 bytes each plus 2048 block-light and 2048 sky-light nibbles; ground-up chunks append 256 biome bytes. The data field is zlib-compressed as a whole, so the client must inflate it before touching any block. A ground-up packet with bitmask 0 means chunk unload, not empty data. S26PacketMapChunkBulk reuses S21PacketChunkData.Extracted for the bulk variant.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats never measure S21; the server cannot tell what the client rendered. Chunk-based cheats (XRay, cave finder) are undetectable server-side in principle, which is why they are banned by staff rather than flagged. The client-side risk is stability: malformed or flooded chunk data crashes the vanilla handler, the basis of chunk-ban exploits that server plugins mitigate by validating senders.
implementation.general_hooks: No module in the 8 clients registers a receive handler for S21. Rise 6.x exposes the class to scripts via NetworkAPI; all other references are vanilla net/minecraft files.
implementation.client_variations: All 8 clients ship the vanilla handleChunkData. Rise 6.1.30/6.2.4 additionally list the class in NetworkAPI; Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity differ only in the bundled vanilla source revision.
